newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY COMMISSION DEEMS MATRA MISSILE DEAL ILLEGAL.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY COMMISSION DEEMS MATRA MISSILE DEAL ILLEGAL.

text.p: France's Matra Defense's $100 million air defence missile deal with Hungary was thrown into confusion on Thursday when an independent commission declared the contract illegal

After six hours of deliberations, the Public Procurement Arbitration Commission, set up to monitor government procurements from abroad, decided the Defence Ministry had contravened the Procurement law when it pursued talks exclusively with Matra after February 20, Hungarian television's evening news reported.
The Defence Ministry announced om Wednesday that Matra had won the deal the deal to deliver three mobile batteries of air defence missiles by the end of the century.
The deal includes an offset deal to cover both investment in and purchases from Hungary's manufacturing sector equivalent to the purchase price, the first such offset deal Hungary has signed.
The ministry's head of procurement Jeno Kopasz expressed surprise at the decision and said the ministry would appeal.
"It is possible to take this to a higher court and this is what we will do," he said.
Hungary, which started the modernisation of its army with a view to NATO membership, announced the first tender for the anti-aircraft missiles last September.
The other bidders were Daimler-Benz , Sweden's Bofors, Bombardier unit Short Brothers of Northern Ireland and Hughes Electronics of the U.S.
Short Brothers' legal representative in Hungary Geza Patay said the company was studying the verdict before deciding what to do next.
"Short's management is considering whether to go to court or not," lawyer Geza Patay said. "We would like first of all to see the decision in writing."
